description: This post provides administrative support to the Palliative Care Team based at North Middlesex University Hospital. The post-holder will provide a high-quality administrative service and patient coordination system to the multidisciplinary specialist palliative care team. The post-holder will work within the teams to coordinate the non-clinical aspects of the services including data input and office management support. He / she will need to be able to organise and prioritise their own workload, use initiative and work without constant supervision. The administrator will work across the two services on allocated days and be required to use Careflow and other electronic databases to capture referrals and procedural information. The post holder will be required to: Ordering of all stationaries on Pecos. Ordering of all information leaflets (booklets /forms DWP, CMC). Emailing urgent letters to GP and other professionals Collection and distribution of all post & letters into the department. Update attendance records in excel for MDT. Room bookings/ circulation to team members for meetings. Contact other NHS and private healthcare providers for patient information for emergency admissions and updating with discharge summaries. Ensure all enquiries from other hospitals are effectively managed by being successfully resolved or escalated to the CNS's Ensure all relevant people are informed and an appropriate record is maintained liaising and effectively communicating at all levels using written, oral and electronic methods. Use tact and sensitivity to deal with difficult issues. Request clinical data sets from other healthcare providers hospitals in accordance in a timely manner. The post holder will provide comprehensive administrative and patient coordination support to the multidisciplinary Specialist Palliative Care Team across North Middlesex University Hospital and associated services. The role is essential in ensuring the efficient operation of the service by managing administrative processes, coordinating referrals, maintaining accurate records, and supporting communication between healthcare professionals, patients, carers, and external organisations. The post holder will work independently, prioritising their workload effectively while ensuring high standards of accuracy, confidentiality, and professionalism. They will contribute to the smooth running of the service through effective office management and administrative support. Provide a high-quality administrative service to the Specialist Palliative Care Team. Act as the first point of contact for telephone, email, and face-to-face enquiries, ensuring queries are resolved appropriately or escalated when necessary. Manage incoming and outgoing correspondence, including the collection, distribution, and filing of post and letters. Prepare, format, distribute, and electronically file correspondence, reports, minutes, and other service documentation. Maintain efficient filing systems in accordance with Trust policies and information governance requirements. Organise and coordinate meetings, including room bookings, diary management, preparation and circulation of meeting agendas and papers. Record and maintain attendance registers and multidisciplinary team (MDT) records using Excel and other electronic systems. Order and monitor stationery and departmental supplies using approved procurement systems, including PECOS. Receive, process, and coordinate referrals to the Specialist Palliative Care Team using Careflow and other electronic patient record systems. Ensure accurate and timely data entry of referrals, patient information, and service activity. Track referrals and ensure relevant information is available to clinical staff in a timely manner. Liaise with patients, carers, healthcare professionals, GPs, hospitals, hospices, and community services to facilitate effective communication and coordination of care. Obtain patient information, discharge summaries, and clinical documentation from NHS and independent healthcare providers where required. Request and manage clinical datasets and supporting information from external organisations in accordance with Trust policies and information governance requirements. Communicate effectively with internal and external stakeholders at all levels using telephone, written, and electronic communication methods. Ensure urgent correspondence, including clinical letters and discharge-related communications, is transmitted promptly to GPs and other healthcare professionals. Provide administrative support for multidisciplinary meetings and service activities. Ensure all enquiries from healthcare providers are managed efficiently and escalated appropriately to Clinical Nurse Specialists or other members of the multidisciplinary team when required. Use tact, diplomacy, and sensitivity when dealing with difficult or sensitive situations involving patients, relatives, carers, and professionals. Maintain accurate and up-to-date patient and service records on Careflow and other electronic databases. Produce routine reports and activity data as required by the service. Ensure compliance with Trust policies relating to confidentiality, data protection, information governance, and record keeping. Monitor and maintain data quality standards to support service reporting and performance monitoring. Support the day-to-day operational management of the office environment. Ensure information leaflets, patient information booklets, DWP forms, Coordinate My Care (CMC) documents, and other service resources are ordered, maintained, and readily available. Assist with service audits, data collection exercises, and quality improvement initiatives as required. Contribute to the continuous improvement of administrative processes and systems to enhance service efficiency and patient experience. Prioritise and organise workload independently, using initiative and judgement where appropriate. Work flexibly across both Specialist Palliative Care services as required by service need. Adhere to all Trust policies, procedures, and statutory requirements. Participate in mandatory training, appraisal, and personal development activities. Maintain professional standards at all times and contribute positively to the objectives of the Specialist Palliative Care Service.

title: Bank Administrator
description: An opportunity has arisen to join the Kingston and Richmond Autism Service in a bank role as an Administrator within the Neurodevelopmental Service. Based at Hollyfield House, you will have a key role in the effective running of a busy service, with responsibilities including referral management, clinical appointments and supporting clinicians within the service. You will also answer queries about the service and will be confident and willing to communicate with neurodivergent people by telephone and face to face, as required. You will need to be well organised in managing clinic appointments, booking and review systems, and coordinating and sending out reports. You will be well supported and highly valued by the Autism Service and will receive regular supervision. The successful applicant will also provide some administrative support to the Adult ADHD Service, as directed by the service leads. Please apply using the NHS Jobs online system. Your application should explain why you are applying for the post, how you believe you would contribute to working in this setting and demonstrate how you meet the requirements of the person specification. Please be aware that the closing date may be brought forward in the event of a high number of applications. Were looking for someone who Has strong administrative and organisational skills, with excellent attention to detail. Can manage competing priorities and work calmly and efficiently in a busy service. Communicates clearly, sensitively and confidently by telephone, email and face to face. Understands the importance of confidentiality, accurate record keeping and timely information sharing. Works well independently and as part of a multidisciplinary team. Ideally has previous administrative experience within a neurodevelopmental, mental health or healthcare service. The usual working hours are 9am- 5pm and will be Monday Friday and there is some flexibility on the days the hours are worked. You will be based at Hollyfield Road in Surbiton although you will also need to be able to travel to our other sites as needed. The successful candidate will be the first point of contact for patients, providing a professional, welcoming and efficient reception service. The role involves face-to-face, telephone and online patient enquiries, appointment administration and general administrative duties to support the smooth day-to-day running of the practice. The ideal candidate will have excellent communication and customer service skills, a calm and professional manner, and the ability to work effectively in a busy environment while maintaining patient confidentiality and delivering a high standard of care. 1. Patient Reception and Customer Service Welcome patients and visitors in a friendly, professional and courteous manner. Check patients in for appointments and update their arrival status on the clinical system. Respond to patient enquiries in person, by telephone and through online communication channels. Assist patients with appointment bookings, cancellations and rearrangements in line with practice procedures. Treat all patients with dignity, respect, sensitivity and confidentiality. Communicate effectively with patients from diverse cultural and linguistic backgrounds. Manage difficult or distressed patients calmly and professionally, escalating concerns when necessary. Ensure patients who require additional assistance are supported appropriately. 2. Telephone and Appointment Management Answer incoming telephone calls promptly and professionally. Handle appointment requests in accordance with practice policies and access procedures. Direct calls to the appropriate member of the clinical or administrative team. Take accurate messages and ensure they are passed to the relevant person in a timely manner. Explain practice procedures, appointment arrangements and available services clearly. Recognise when a call may require urgent clinical attention and follow the practice's approved escalation procedures. Never provide clinical advice beyond the receptionist's level of training and authorised responsibilities. Use the practice's clinical computer system, SystmOne, Use the practice's clinical computer system, such as EMIS Web or SystmOne, as applicable. Report any data breaches, confidentiality concerns or incidents to the Practice Manager promptly. Assist colleagues during periods of high demand and provide appropriate cover when required. Undertake other reasonable duties consistent with the role and level of responsibility.

To book patients into available appointments either by telephone or in person following the current practice protocol and when requested by a member of the medical staff. 6. To undertake to answer the telephone promptly, taking clear and accurate messages where necessary, ensuring that messages are passed to the correct person in an approved manner for patients of the practice and for the travel clinic. 7. To undertake to print and prepare repeat prescriptions ready for signature by a doctor. 8. To undertake to issue repeat prescriptions and other reports, forms, and letters, etc., to patients that are ready for collection. 9. To collect monies from patients for items for which a patient charge applies. 10. To undertake to assist or aid patients with disabilities as and when required. 11. To undertake to act as a chaperone to a patient if required to do so by a doctor or nurse. 12. To undertake to book transport for patients when appropriate. 13. To answer the results line, deal appropriately with result requests, both in person, and by telephone. 14. To undertake to process New Registrations. 15. To report any potentially aggressive incidents, difficulties with the client group or accidents in the first instant to the Patient Services Manager, or Practice Manager for appropriate action. 16. To undertake to be aware of any potential security breaches of the building whilst on duty. 17. To ensure that the premises are securely locked at the end of the working day; ensuring that doors to rooms not in use are closed; that the Library and Seminar room doors are locked and all windows are securely closed and locked where appropriate. 18. To ensure to the appropriate message is displayed on front door/gate when the premises are closed. 19. To ensure that the premises are kept tidy and that magazines and leaflets within the waiting area are tidied prior to the commencement and at the end of each clinical session. 20. To assist in maintaining a clean and safe environment for staff, patients and users of the practice. 21. To use the computer system appropriately and be able to re-start/re-boot an individual computer workstation should it be necessary. OTHER DUTIES The following lists of duties are to be carried out by Patient Services Team. No Patient Services Team members should carry out any of the following duties unless they have been specifically trained. These duties are not in any order and may be allocated to one or more persons. Specific Duties: 1. To undertake Child Immunisation and Vaccination target work as and when required. 2. To undertake Cervical Screening target work as and when required. 3. To undertake the scanning of patient's results and any other patient correspondence into the patients' computerised records. 4. To undertake to process and return patient records to and from Primary Care Support England (NHS England). 5. To ensure that all temporary resident claims and immediate necessary claims have been made. 6. To undertake to ensure that newly registered patients' records are matched/married to their existing health record when it arrives from Primary Care Support England (NHS England) 7. To undertake to monitor and assist with two week wait referrals promptly via the e-Referral system 8. To open external post and post from Royal Free Hospital on a daily basis, date stamp and distribute as per the practice protocol 9. To provide support to the management team as and when required The allocation of duties will be by the Practice Manager or Patient Services Manager and staff will be expected to take on additional duties or relinquish existing duties to ensure the efficient running of the practice. Requests for such changes, when they occur should not reasonably be refused. This job description is not meant to be exhaustive and may change with the agreement of the Practice Manager and the post holder. The agreement to any change by the post holder should not be reasonably withheld.

title: Medical Receptionist

The role includes both front desk and back office duties. Hours by mutual agreement to be part of a team of six staff covering 0745 to 1830, Monday to Friday. Receive, assist and direct patients in accessing the appropriate service or healthcare professional in a courteous, efficient and effective way. Carry out administrative tasks relating to patient records, including filing, document management and ensuring patients can access reports, prescriptions and that they are easily accessible. Give administrative support to the clinicians, practice manager and reception manager where appropriate and as requested. Provide general assistance to the practice team and project a positive and friendly image to patients and other visitors, either in person or via the telephone. Follow practice protocols to ensure consistent and high quality care is provided to our patients. To have a thorough knowledge of all practice procedures To work in accordance of written protocols Scan incoming post and other documents for electronic filing of clinical correspondence Action third party requests for medical records in accordance with practice protocol Prepare and open up practice at start of day when on early duty Greet & receive patients, consulting with members of practice team Check patients in on arrival using the practice computer system (EMIS) or direct them to self-check in. Oversee the reception area in such a way that ensures all patients are seen in turn Deal with prescriptions Be able to cover all reception tasks as necessary Close and secure practice at end of day when on late duty Process appointment requests for today/future appointments from patients by telephone and in person using the practice computer system (EMIS) Registrations of new regular patients and temporary patients computer data entry and medical records Maintain working knowledge of telephone system Answer telephone calls to the practice dealing with enquiries, fielding calls where appropriate or taking messages using the practice electronic message book Sort and date stamp all incoming patient-related mail Scan patient-related documents onto medical records using read codes as agreed by the clinical team Forward relevant documents to the doctor or nurse Ensure incoming letters are scanned onto the patient record Scan all internal paper documents on to the relevant patients record and then store the documents in line with practice procedure

title: Care Navigator/Receptionist & Administrator
description: As the first point of contact for patients, you will play a key role in delivering excellent customer service and supporting the smooth running of the practice. Duties include welcoming patients, handling telephone and face-to-face enquiries, responding to emails, processing prescription requests, filing and coding clinical correspondence and referrals, supporting safeguarding processes, undertaking site checks, monitoring stock levels, and helping maintain a safe environment. Working as part of a team of four, you will contribute to a shared workload and help ensure patients receive the right support at the right time. The role is offered on a split rota of 07:45-13:45 (Week 1) and 13:00-19:00 (Week 2) . Previous experience in a GP practice or similar patient-facing role is essential. Applicants must have 6-12 months' experience and be proficient in EMIS Web . The successful candidate must deliver excellent patient care and customer service while maintaining professionalism and accuracy. If you are a reliable team player with excellent communication skills, attention to detail and a commitment to patient care, we would love to hear from you. As a Patient Care Navigator / Receptionist / Administrator, you will be the first point of contact for patients and visitors, providing a professional, friendly and efficient service. You will welcome patients, respond to enquiries in person and by telephone, and support patients in accessing the most appropriate services. The role includes processing prescription requests, responding to emails, filing and coding clinical correspondence, maintaining accurate patient records, processing referrals via NHS e-Referral Service, actioning eConsults as directed by the clinical team, managing appointments, registering new patients, and handling general enquiries. You will be expected to cover colleagues' absences where required, attend practice meetings, maintain a tidy reception area, support patient recall programmes, and undertake additional administrative tasks as directed by the Practice Manager. You will support safeguarding processes, undertake site checks, monitor stock levels, report issues appropriately, and help ensure the premises are safe and secure. Working as part of a team of four, you will share workloads, support colleagues during busy periods, and contribute to a positive, patient-focused environment. Excellent communication skills, attention to detail, flexibility and a commitment to high-quality patient care are essential. Job description Key Responsibilities Patient Care & Reception Meet and greet patients and visitors in a professional and welcoming manner. Assist patients with enquiries, signposting them to the most appropriate service where necessary. Respond to patient queries both in person and over the telephone. Support patients with appointments, registrations and general practice services. Always maintain patient confidentiality. Administrative Duties Process incoming hospital correspondence, including filing and clinical coding of letters and reports. Process prescription requests accurately and efficiently. Respond promptly to emails received by the practice. Maintain accurate patient records and update information as required. Undertake general administrative tasks to support the smooth running of the practice. Safeguarding & Compliance Identify and escalate any safeguarding concerns or requests appropriately. Follow all practice policies, procedures and information governance requirements. Support the practice in maintaining a safe environment for patients, staff and visitors. Premises & Operational Support Carry out routine site and building checks as required. Ensure the building is secure at opening and closing times. Monitor and maintain appropriate stock levels of clinical and office supplies. Report maintenance issues or concerns promptly. Teamworking Work collaboratively as part of a team of four within the reception and administration function. Support colleagues during busy periods and contribute positively to team objectives. Participate fully in the shared workload and demonstrate flexibility where required. Promote a positive, patient-focused culture throughout the practice.

title: GP Receptionist
description: Join Dr Sharma & Rai Practice Group as a full-time GP Receptionist, primarily based at Heathway Medical Centre in Dagenham. You will be a welcoming first point of contact for patients and a valued member of our friendly and supportive practice team. We are looking for someone reliable, organised and confident communicating with people face to face. Previous GP reception experience is an advantage, but not essential. We also welcome applicants with strong customer service experience who enjoy helping people, can manage a variety of tasks and are quick to learn new online systems. Good IT skills, excellent communication and a friendly, professional approach are essential. This is a fixed-term position until 8 August 2027, with the possibility of extension. The role is 37.5 hours per week, working varied shifts between 07:45 and 18:30, Monday to Friday, excluding bank holidays. Pay is £12.71 per hour. Our wider practice group offers opportunities to gain experience, develop new skills and apply for permanent positions as vacancies arise. We reserve the right to close this vacancy early if sufficient applications are received. Early applications are encouraged. As a GP Receptionist, you will play an important role in supporting patients and helping the practice run smoothly. Your daily responsibilities will include: Welcoming patients and visitors, providing friendly and professional assistance. Responding to patient enquiries face to face, by telephone and through online systems. Helping patients access appropriate services, including assisting with online appointment requests. Using our clinical system (EMIS Web) and other digital platforms to manage patient information and administrative tasks. Processing patient requests, including prescriptions, test-related enquiries and general correspondence. Supporting GPs, nurses and other team members with day-to-day administrative duties. Maintaining accurate records and handling confidential information appropriately. Working closely with colleagues to provide a positive experience for patients. Full training and guidance on our practice systems and procedures will be provided. We value teamwork, initiative and a willingness to learn. Job Description GP Receptionist Organisation: Dr Sharma & Rai Practice Group Primary Location: Heathway Medical Centre, Dagenham Contract: Full-time, fixed-term until 8 August 2027, with the possibility of extension Hours: 37.5 hours per week, with varied shifts between 07:45 and 18:30, Monday to Friday, excluding bank holidays. To provide a friendly, professional and efficient reception and administrative service to patients, visitors and healthcare professionals. The GP Receptionist plays an important role in supporting patients to access healthcare services, maintaining accurate records and assisting the wider practice team with daily operations. The successful candidate will be based primarily at Heathway Medical Centre, with occasional cover at other practices within Dr Sharma & Rai Practice Group where required. 1. Patient Reception and Customer Service Welcome patients and visitors in a friendly, helpful and professional manner. Act as a first point of contact for patients attending the practice. Respond to patient enquiries face to face, by telephone and through digital communication systems. Assist patients with appointment requests and provide information about available services. Support patients who may require additional assistance accessing healthcare services. Communicate clearly and sensitively with patients from different backgrounds and with varying needs. Handle patient concerns and difficult situations calmly, professionally and respectfully, referring matters to senior colleagues when appropriate. Maintain a welcoming, organised and professional reception environment. 2. Appointment Management and Patient Access Support patients with accessing appointments and services in accordance with practice procedures. Assist patients in using online consultation and appointment request systems. Provide guidance on accessing the NHS App and other available digital services. Process appointment requests, cancellations and changes as directed by practice procedures. Signpost patients to appropriate services using established practice guidance and care navigation procedures. Escalate urgent concerns or clinical queries to the appropriate healthcare professional without providing clinical advice. Help ensure patients receive clear and accurate information about practice services. 3. Clinical Systems and Digital Administration Use EMIS Web and other practice systems to access and update patient information accurately. Process patient requests received through online platforms and electronic communication systems. Scan, upload and attach relevant documents to patient records. Record patient interactions and administrative activities appropriately. Support the processing of incoming correspondence and electronic documents. Maintain accurate records while following confidentiality and information governance requirements. Learn and confidently use new digital systems as introduced by the practice. 4. General Administrative Duties Process routine patient enquiries relating to prescriptions, test requests, referrals and other practice services in accordance with established procedures. Assist with the collection and distribution of forms, letters and other documents. Support the preparation and processing of administrative correspondence. Liaise with hospitals, pharmacies, community healthcare providers and other external organisations when required. Maintain accurate records and ensure administrative tasks are completed in a timely manner. Support clinical and non-clinical colleagues with general administrative tasks. Assist with maintaining an organised and efficient reception and office environment. 5. Teamwork and Communication Work collaboratively with reception colleagues, GPs, nurses, healthcare assistants and administrative staff. Communicate effectively with colleagues to support the smooth running of the practice. Provide reception cover and assistance to colleagues when required. Share relevant information with appropriate team members to ensure continuity of service. Participate in team meetings, training and development activities. Contribute positively to a respectful, supportive and professional working environment. 6. Confidentiality, Safety and Professional Standards Maintain strict patient confidentiality and comply with data protection and information governance requirements. Follow practice policies and procedures, including safeguarding, health and safety, infection prevention and control, and equality and diversity. Recognise and appropriately escalate safeguarding concerns or situations requiring clinical attention. Treat all patients, visitors and colleagues with dignity, respect and sensitivity. Full induction and training on practice-specific systems and procedures will be provided. Previous experience in a GP practice and familiarity with EMIS Web would be advantageous but are not essential. We welcome candidates with experience in customer-facing roles who demonstrate strong communication skills, a positive attitude, good computer skills and a willingness to learn. As part of Dr Sharma & Rai Practice Group, employees may have opportunities to develop additional skills, gain experience across different practice functions and apply for permanent vacancies as they arise. The successful candidate must be flexible in their working hours and available for different shifts within the practice's core opening hours. title: GP Receptionist
description: Join our friendly team at St Katharine Docks Practice , a welcoming single-handed GP surgery set in the beautiful surroundings of St Katharine Docks, just moments from the Tower of London. We pride ourselves on providing high-quality, personalised care to our patients and creating a supportive, professional, and inclusive workplace. We are looking for a Receptionist to provide cover , helping to ensure the smooth running of our busy front desk. As the first point of contact for patients, youll play a vital role in making every patient feel welcome, listened to, and supported. Youll handle calls, manage appointments, process correspondence, and assist the GP and wider team in delivering excellent service. This role is ideal for someone who enjoys helping others, communicates clearly and kindly, and can stay calm under pressure. Youll need to be organised, confident using computers, and committed to maintaining confidentiality at all times. In return, we offer a friendly working environment, on-the-job training, and opportunities for personal development. Youll be part of a small, close-knit team where your contribution truly makes a difference to the lives of our patients and the success of our practice. If youre reliable, compassionate, and looking for a rewarding role in the heart of London, wed love to hear from you. Welcome and assist patients and visitors in person and over the telephone in a professional and friendly manner. Manage incoming calls, respond to general enquiries, and direct calls as appropriate. Schedule and manage patient appointments using the practice clinical system - EMIS Web. Register new patients and update existing patient information accurately. Handle incoming and outgoing post and emails. Obtain external medical reports, test results, and other documentation as required. Scan and file correspondence and clinical documents. Maintain a tidy, organised, and welcoming reception area. Safeguard patient confidentiality and comply with GDPR and NHS data protection requirements. Provide reassurance and support to patients, maintaining a calm and caring approach. Carry out general administrative duties as required by the GP or Practice Manager. Ensure an effective and efficient reception service is provided to patients and any other visitors to the Practice. Deal with all general enquiries, explain procedures and make new and follow-up appointments. Using your own judgment and communication skills ensure that patients with no prior appointment but who need urgent consultation are seen in a logical and non-disruptive manner. Explain Practice arrangements and formal requirements to new patients and those seeking temporary cover and ensure procedures are completed. Receive and make telephone calls as required. Divert calls and take messages, ensuring accuracy of detail and prompt appropriate delivery. Enter requests for home visits into the home visits book, ensuring careful recording of all relevant details and where necessary refer to Duty Doctor. Action repeat prescription requests and ensure that they are ready for collection by the patient within 48 hours, in line with Practice protocol. Take action on clinicians requests for further information/patient contact information etc. including computerised practice notes, ensuring completion of all associated paperwork. Advise patients of relevant charges for private (non-General Medical Services) services, accept payment and issue receipts for same. Enter patient information on to the computer as required. Prepare clinical rooms for surgeries, supply prescription forms and record numbers in use and ensure adequate supplies of consumables - including bottles, couch rolls, test request forms etc..

title: Medical Receptionist
description: The Law Medical Group Practice is seeking a reliable and organised Receptionist to join the team at its Wembley branch. The successful candidate will play a key role in supporting the clinical and non clinical teams by undertaking a range of front of house and administrative duties. The role will involve full front of house responsibilities, including welcoming and directing patients, responding to queries and providing a professional and efficient service both in person and over the telephone. Working Pattern: Part Time, 27.5 Hours per Week The working hours are Monday to Friday, 1:00 pm to 6:30 pm. Please note: The working days and hours are non negotiable . Applicants must be able to commit to this working pattern. Eligibility: Applicants must be UK citizens and have a minimum of five years of work experience in the UK. The role involves providing comprehensive reception support to the multidisciplinary team within the practice. Key responsibilities include managing patient interactions, handling incoming correspondence, and ensuring accurate distribution of information to clinicians. The position includes front-desk duties such as greeting and directing patients, managing the appointment system using EMIS , booking appointments, responding to patient enquiries, and supporting the smooth and efficient day-to-day operation of the practice. Scan and upload documents onto the EMIS clinical system, ensuring accurate patient record management. Review and appropriately allocate documents within EMIS , forwarding them to the relevant clinician for review and action. Initiate and respond to requests from patients, practice staff, and external healthcare agencies in a professional and timely manner. Photocopy and prepare documentation as required by clinicians and practice staff. Provide cover for colleagues during periods of absence to ensure continuity of service. Accurately input patient information and updates into EMIS where required. Manage and resolve patient queries efficiently, escalating issues where appropriate. Maintain a clean, organised, and efficient reception environment at all times. Support the clinical team with day-to-day operational tasks as required. Complete tasks relating to patient results, correspondence, and clinical letters where appropriate. Process incoming electronic communications and documents where required. Scan and attach patient-related documentation accurately to patient records within EMIS . Carry out opening and closing procedures in accordance with the practice rota and operational requirements.

title: Personal Assistant
description: As Personal Assistant (PA) to the Patient Experience Director (PED) the post holder will provide comprehensive administrative and business support, ensuring the Director's responsibilities are effectively managed. This includes managing a complex diary, correspondence, communication, coordination and delegation ensuring the Director receives a consistent and high-level of support. The post holder will work closely with key colleagues and the senior leadership team to the Director. They will play a crucial role in ensuring the smooth and efficient operation of the Director's office, enabling the Director to focus on their extensive core responsibilities. As PA you will need to be confident to self-initiate tasks, be a clear communicator and comfortable operating efficiently and effectively in a high-pressure environment. Please be aware that should you be successful in this position, you will be hired to the job title of Personal Assistant, and this job title is advertised to attract the right skills needed for the role. We are looking for an experienced personal assistant who is a strong team player, highly organised, and who has the ability to communicate effectively and professionally with a wide range of people. Your duties will include but not limited to; Complex diary and mailbox managementMeeting coordinationTravel arrangementsMonitoring and recording of annual leave/absencesEntering expense claims for DirectorRespond to ad-hoc, non-routine requests by the Director and their direct reports effectively, professionally and in good time. Detailed job description and main responsibilities Key responsibilities as PA to Director; Diary Management: Managing a complex diary, balancing competing priorities, and coordinating travel arrangements. Meeting Coordination: Preparing agendas, taking minutes, and following up on action items. Correspondence: Handling internal and external communications, including emails and written correspondence. Information Dissemination: Ensuring accurate and timely dissemination of information to relevant parties. Administrative Support: Providing general administrative support, such as filing, data entry, and photocopying. Team Support: Supporting other administrative staff and providing assistance when needed. Confidentiality: Maintaining confidentiality of sensitive information. Communication and Interpersonal Skills: Effectively communicating with a wide range of individuals, both internally and externally. Organisation and Time Management: Managing workload effectively, prioritising tasks, and meeting deadlines. You can find further details about the role, including key responsibilities and accountabilities, alongside the organisational structure and person specification in the attached Job Description and other supporting documents. Applicants from within the NHS will be offered on a secondment basis only, agreement should be obtained from their employer prior to submitting the application.

title: GP Receptionist
description: We are offering an exciting opportunity to join our hardworking and welcoming GP Practice as a Receptionist, providing vital support and becoming an integral part of our dedicated Team. In this part-time role, no two days are ever the same youll be helping patients, solving problems, and making a real difference in peoples lives. Alongside greeting patients, managing appointments, and handling enquiries with care, youll also take on some important administrative tasks that keep the practice running smoothly. This role comes with full training, so no formal qualifications are required. However, previous experience in a GP practice would be preferential but what matters most is your enthusiasm, reliability, and willingness to learn. What you will be doing day to day As a GP Receptionist, you will be at the heart of our practice, making a real difference to patients and the team. Your role will be varied, rewarding, and sometimes challenging - but always important. Help patients feel supported by managing appointments, processing referrals, and guiding them through their healthcare journey. Keep communication flowing between patients and healthcare professionals, ensuring everyone has the information they need. Take on key admin tasks that keep the practice running smoothly, from handling queries to maintaining accurate records. Champion safety and standards by following procedures, keeping the environment clean and safe, and supporting governance responsibilities. This is a role where youll be helping people every day, working in a supportive team, and knowing that your contribution truly makes a difference. What youll be doing As a GP Receptionist, youll be the first point of contact for patients and play a key role in keeping the practice running smoothly. Book, change, or cancel appointments and help patients with referrals. Guide patients to the right healthcare professional or service. Arrange home visits when needed and follow simple triage steps. Keep the reception area clean and safe so patients feel comfortable. Spot and report problems to the Deputy Practice Manager. Keep accurate records of patient interactions. Register new patients and update records. Scan and process documents and use clinical IT systems. Use resources wisely and avoid unnecessary waste.

title: Practice Administrator
description: We are looking for an organised, motivated and proactive individual to join The Wapping Group Practice and take the lead in managing our QOF, LES and patient recall systems. This is a temporary maternity cover position, with a fixed-term contract of at least 13 months. Flexible working hours: 25 to 37.5 hours per week . This is an important role within our practice, ensuring patients receive the care they need while helping us achieve our clinical and contractual targets. You will work closely with our clinical, administrative and PCN teams to coordinate recalls, monitor performance, improve processes and ensure accurate clinical coding. We offer a friendly and supportive working environment where you will have the opportunity to take ownership of your work, develop your skills and make a real difference to patient care and practice performance. We will provide the necessary training and support to help you succeed in this role, so you do not need to have experience in every aspect of the job. We are looking for someone who is willing to learn, takes initiative and is committed to delivering high-quality work. The successful candidate will be responsible for overseeing the practice's QOF, LES and patient recall systems, ensuring patients are contacted, booked and followed up appropriately. The role involves monitoring performance against clinical targets, coordinating recall activities with the administrative and PCN teams, managing appointment availability and ensuring accurate clinical coding on EMIS. You will also oversee childhood immunisation and cervical screening recalls, identify areas for improvement and work closely with the clinical team to maximise practice performance. Key Responsibilities QOF, LES and Target Management Manage and coordinate all QOF, LES and other contractual recall activities to ensure the practice achieves maximum performance against targets. Monitor QOF and LES dashboards regularly, identifying areas where performance needs improvement. Take responsibility for managing all targets comprehensively, ensuring patients are recalled, booked and appropriately coded. Regularly update EMIS searches and review performance dashboards to identify outstanding work and missed opportunities. Work closely with the clinical and administrative teams to ensure all targets are achieved within the required deadlines. Patient Recall Management Manage the practice's recall system from start to finish, ensuring eligible patients are identified, contacted, booked and followed up. Generate, distribute and monitor recall lists, ensuring work is completed accurately and on time. Allocate recall lists to PCN recall staff, monitor their progress and follow up on outstanding tasks. Ensure patients who do not respond to initial recall attempts are followed up appropriately. Send validation letters to patients who have not responded after repeated contact attempts, in line with practice protocols. Ensure accurate records are maintained of all recall attempts, patient responses and outcomes. Clinical Appointment Management Review and adjust clinical appointment sessions on EMIS, adding or removing appointment slots where necessary to support QOF and LES recall activities. Ensure sufficient clinical appointments are available for patients requiring reviews, monitoring, vaccinations and other target-related activities. Liaise with clinicians and the management team to plan appointment capacity according to recall demand and outstanding targets. Clinical Coding and Data Quality Ensure all QOF and LES activities are accurately coded on EMIS to support correct reporting and achievement. Identify missing or incorrect clinical codes and liaise with the relevant clinicians to resolve any issues. Provide training and guidance to administrative and recall staff on correct clinical coding procedures. Keep staff updated on changes to QOF, LES and other relevant coding requirements. Carry out regular data quality checks to ensure completed clinical activities are correctly recorded and reflected in performance reports. Childhood Immunisations and Cervical Screening Manage childhood immunisation recalls and targets, ensuring eligible children are identified, contacted and followed up. Monitor childhood immunisation performance and work with the clinical team to improve uptake and achieve contractual targets. Manage cervical screening recalls comprehensively, ensuring eligible patients are invited, booked and appropriately followed up. Monitor cervical screening uptake and identify patients who are overdue or have not responded to invitations. Ensure cervical screening records are accurately maintained, including coding of colposcopy correspondence and relevant clinical outcomes. Ensure cervical screening referral information is correctly recorded and processed through CSMS where required. Work closely with the clinical team to resolve coding discrepancies and ensure screening activity is accurately reflected in EMIS and performance dashboards. Staff Coordination and Training Coordinate the work of PCN recall staff by allocating tasks, setting priorities and monitoring progress. Provide regular feedback and guidance to ensure recall activities are completed efficiently. Train staff on recall procedures, EMIS searches, clinical coding and changes to contractual requirements. Maintain effective communication between clinical, administrative and PCN teams to ensure a coordinated approach to achieving practice targets. Identify areas for improvement and implement changes to strengthen recall processes and overall performance. Performance Monitoring and Reporting Regularly review QOF, LES, childhood immunisation and cervical screening performance. Identify gaps in achievement and take proactive steps to improve performance before contractual deadlines. Provide regular progress updates to the Practice Manager, highlighting outstanding targets, risks and areas requiring additional support. Ensure the practice maximises appropriate contractual achievement and income through effective recall management, accurate coding and timely completion of clinical activities.

title: Patient Care Administrator
description: Job summary This post requires someone with initiative, enthusiasm, excellent communication skills and empathy with patients and colleagues. Well organised, reliable and with a flexible approach to team work. The role involves reception and admin duties both patient facing and over the phone. You will liaise with team members to provide a reception service including answering patient and visitor general enquires and booking appointments. Admin duties will include patient records maintenance, recording repeat prescriptions and processing patient emails received via the surgery website all in accordance with protocols. You will be required to ensure the professional image of the practice is maintained whilst acting as the first point of contact with patients and visitors. Main duties of the job The successful candidate will: Have experience of working with others Be highly motivated and innovative self starter Be discreet and able to maintain confidentiality Have a professional and personable presentation and demeanour Have excellent customer service skills and ability to communicate confidently with the general public over the phone and face to face Excellent communication skills and the ability to problem solve and resolve issues calmly under pressure It literate with a high standard of accuracy and quality Information management- able to collect, organise and input data efficiently Time Management: able to work to deadlines **3 COVID-19 VACCINE MANDATORY ** Must be available to start at 8.00am and / or finish at 19.00pm Job Responsibilities Reception To liaise with team members in providing a reception service Respond and redirect all patient and visitor requests accordingly Receive incoming telephone calls, answer general enquiries and transfer or document calls and messages as appropriate. Book in patients based on the reception script and visitors in line with practice appointments and visitors procedures. To be aware of other local resources and community organisations, and provide information to patients. Collect payments from patients for non-NHS services. To provide cover for colleagues on leave. This will include cover for late/early shifts. Admin Receive and record requests for repeat prescriptions in line with the set protocol Distribute mail as appropriate and open all incoming general mail and mail for clinicians (unless marked personal or instructed otherwise). Sort out all patient correspondence in line with protocols. To scan all patient correspondence onto the computer, process correspondence for actioning. To archive old patient correspondence. To process emails received from patients via the surgery website. Record all requests for medical reports. Register new patients according to the practice area onto EMIS computer system. Amend patients records to show change of name, address etc. onto the computer system, checking if these changes apply to others in the household. To send out appointment letters, or contact patients by telephone to change or book appointments. To be responsible for allocated personal tasks towards target achievement. To cover the personal tasks of other reception staff during periods of leave. To collect and provide audit data. To be aware of, and to operate within, practice protocols and guidelines - e.g. confidentiality, health & safety. Services Ensure that the professional image of the practice is maintained through the highest standards of staff behaviour and appearance and the look/appearance of waiting-room facilities. Attend to and resolve any ad hoc issues and problems as they arise in the day-to-day running of reception. Escalate these to line management where appropriate. Act as the first point of contact in dealing with and resolving complaints about staff or the service. Maintain effective two-way communication with patients and the practice team. Develop own skills to facilitate minor running repairs/fixes to equipment and IT. Develop and assist in the development of protocols, standard procedures and performance standards. Maintain waiting-room notice boards, both electronic and paper. Assist management in interaction with the Patient Participation Group. Attend to or report ad hoc building or facilities issues as they arise in the day-to-day running of the practice. General Deal with general administrative issues related to the reception service. Attend regular and ad hoc staff meetings as required. Provide cover for absent staff when necessary. Undertake other relevant duties assigned by management from time to time in order to ensure the smooth running of the practice. Health and Safety Under the Health and Safety at Work Act 1974, as an employee, you must take reasonable care for the health and safety of yourself and for other persons who may be affected by your acts or omissions at work. The Act also states that you must not intentionally or recklessly interfere with or misuse anything provided in the interests of health, safety and welfare. You will assist in promoting and maintaining your own and others health, safety and security as set out in applicable Practice polices and protocols. This will include: Using personal security systems within the workplace as directed. Identifying risks involved in work activities and managing those risks. Using appropriate infection control procedures, maintaining work areas in a tidy and safe way and free from hazards. Reporting health and safety hazards and infection hazards immediately when recognised. Keeping own work areas and general / patient areas clean and assisting in the maintenance of general standards of cleanliness. Equality and Diversity Morris House is committed to developing, supporting and sustaining a diverse workforce, representative of the community it serves, through the creation of a work environment where staff are able to do their jobs to the best of their abilities without having to face discrimination or harassment. All employeeshave a responsibility to ensure that they understand the standards we expect and to promote and adhere to the policies and measures adopted by the practice. You will support the equality, diversity and rights of patients, carers and colleagues by: Acting in a way that recognizes the importance of peoples rights that is consistent with practice policies and current legislation. Respecting the privacy, dignity, needs and beliefs of patients, carers and colleagues. Behaving in a welcoming manner which is non-judgmental and respects the circumstances, feelings, priorities and rights of others. Vulnerable Adults, Children & Young People All members of staff have a duty to safeguard and promote the welfare of vulnerable adults, children and young people in all relevant areas of their work. This will include timely attendance at relevant training events and compliance with practice procedures. Personal/Professional Development You will participate in any training or development programme implemented by the practice as part of your employment. This will include: Participating in an annual development review including taking responsibility for maintaining a record of your own personal and/or professional development. Taking responsibility for your own development, learning and performance and demonstrating skills and activities to others who are undertaking similar work. Keeping abreast of legislative changes and guidance relating to your role. Quality You will strive to maintain quality within the practice, and will: Alert other team members to issues of quality and risk. Assess your own performance and take accountability for your own actions, either directly or under supervision. Contribute to the effectiveness of the team by reflecting on your own and team activities and making suggestions on ways to improve and enhance the teams performance. Work effectively with individuals in other agencies to meet patients needs. Effectively manage your own time, workload and resources. Communication You should recognize the importance of effective communication within the team and will strive to: Communicate effectively with other team members. Communicate effectively with patients and carers. Recognize peoples needs for alternative methods of communication and respond accordingly.

title: GP Receptionist/Care Navigator
description: ICO Health Group is seeking an experienced and compassionate GP Care Navigator to join our busy and supportive practice team on a 12-month fixed-term contract. As the first point of contact for patients, you will deliver a high-quality, professional front-line service, ensuring patients are directed to the most appropriate healthcare professional or service. This role is key to improving patient access, supporting clinical teams, and maintaining an efficient and responsive service. Patient Care Navigation Act as the first point of contact for patients via face-to-face, telephone, and digital platforms Signpost patients to appropriate clinicians or services, including GPs, nurses, pharmacists, social care, and voluntary organisations Support patients in accessing NHS and community services Promote self-care and patient independence Reception and Administrative Duties Book, amend, and manage appointments and home visit requests Register new and temporary patients Process repeat prescriptions in line with practice protocols Manage incoming and outgoing correspondence, including scanning and filing Clinical Systems & IT Maintain accurate patient records using EMIS Web and other digital systems Use tools such as CHATDOC AI to support patient interactions Support data entry, searches, and reporting requirements Communication & Coordination Liaise with clinicians, healthcare professionals, and external services Communicate effectively with patients and carers Support continuity of care through accurate and timely information sharing Assist in managing the appointment system efficiently Help ensure patients are seen by the most appropriate clinician, reducing GP workload Maintain a clean, organised, and welcoming reception environment Compliance & Governance Adhere to confidentiality, GDPR, and data protection requirements Follow infection control, safeguarding, and health & safety policies Promote equality, diversity, and inclusion Operational Support Team Working & Development Work collaboratively within the practice team Participate in training and ongoing professional development Contribute to service improvement initiatives

title: Medical Receptionist
description: Abbey Medical Centre Camden, London NW8 OAG. We are seeking committed receptionists, who demonstrate enthusiasm for working in primary care, with a genuine interest in working with patients and contributing to the delivery of high quality health care. Applicants should be courteous, highly motivated, pro-active and good team players, able to project a positive and friendly image to patients/visitors. These posts are full time/part time . Each of the posts available may be suitable for job share. Part Time will also be considered (over 5 days). This will involve working on reception (front desk), back office function including processing repeat prescriptions, scanning, summarising, filing medical records.etc. The job will be varied and time will be split between the roles. The surgery uses EMISWeb/DOCMAN 10 as their clinical system. The following are the core responsibilities of the receptionist/administrator. There may be on occasion, a requirement to carry out other tasks; this will be dependent upon factors such as workload and staffing levels: a. Maintaining and monitoring the practice appointment system b. Process personal, telephone and e-requests for appointments c. Answer incoming phone calls, transferring calls or dealing with the callers request appropriately d. Action all incoming faxes e. Signpost patients to the correct service f. Process incoming and outgoing mail g. Initiating contact with and responding to, requests from patients, team members and external agencies h. Process referrals to external agencies such as secondary care using the electronic referral system (ERS) i. Process calling letters are requested j. Process all DNA letters in accordance with current policy k. Action GP2GP tasks l. Read code data on EMIS Web m. Photocopy documentation as required n. File and store records as required o. Data entry of new and temporary registrations and relevant patient information as required p. Input data into the patients healthcare records as necessary q. Scanning of patient related documentation and attaching scanned documents to patients healthcare records r. Process requests for information i.e. SAR, insurance / solicitors letters and DVLA forms to the administrative team s. Manage all queries (including administrative queries) as necessary in an efficient manner t. Carry out system searches as requested u. Maintain a clean, tidy, effective working area at all times v. Monitor and maintain the reception area and notice boards w. Support all clinical staff with general tasks as requested Secondary Responsibilities In addition to the primary responsibilities, the medical administrator may be requested to: a. Partake in audit as directed by the audit lead b. Produce meeting agendas and record the minutes of meetings c. Support administrative and reception staff, providing cover during staff absences d. Complete opening and closing procedures in accordance with the duty rota e. As required support in the management of repeat prescriptions, ensuring they are processed accurately and efficiently f. Ordering and monitoring of stationery supplies

title: Medical Receptionist
description: Fernlea Surgery, is a busy and well-establish GP Practice in South Tottenham, North London, is seeking an enthusiastic Medical Receptionist/Administrator to join our friendly and supportive Medical Administration team. We have an excellent team of GPs and Nurses, a supportive Management Team and efficient administrative team. Our Practice list size is approximately 12,500. We are open to full time and part time applicants and can offer a range of shifts between Monday to Friday. Shifts would range from 8am - 6:30pm with either a 8am start or 1pm. What we offer A competitive salary Paid 30 minute lunch break per day NHS Pension scheme Paid DBS Starting with 20 days annual leave (plus bank holidays) Free on-site car parking Supportive and welcoming team environment Full training and development opportunities Main duties of the job This is a varied, rewarding position in a busy GP practice setting. The Medical Receptionist/Administrator will work across both administrative and reception functions within the practice, providing reliable operational support to clinicians and the wider multidisciplinary team. The role requires an individual who can work confidently with clinical systems, manage competing priorities, and provide a professional patient-facing service while exercising judgement and initiative. Job responsibilities Main duties and responsibilities of the post 1. Administrative and coordination responsibilities Undertake a broad range of administrative duties to support the effective running of the practice Process patient information (electronic and hard copy) accurately, securely, and in a timely manner Monitor, manage, and action incoming emails, electronic tasks, and workflow requests independently Carry out searches, audits, recalls, and administrative reporting as required Type letters, reports, referrals, and associated clinical documentation Respond to administrative requests from clinicians, using judgement to prioritise actions Identify system issues, workflow gaps, or risks and escalate appropriately Report faults to software suppliers and/or IT support and track progress 2. Reception and patient-facing responsibilities Act as a professional and confident point of contact for patients, both face to face and via telephone Respond to patient enquiries using judgement to prioritise urgent, complex, or sensitive matters Support safe navigation of patients to the most appropriate service in line with practice policy Book appointments, recalls, and follow-ups accurately using the computerised appointment system Monitor patient flow and waiting times and escalate concerns appropriately Explain practice procedures, registration processes, and temporary resident arrangements clearly 3. Clinical systems and medical records Assist with the accurate input, updating, and maintenance of patient records on EMIS Clinically code data and correspondence where appropriate Scan, upload, and file patient-related documentation promptly Open, date-stamp, and distribute correspondence, reports, and results to relevant clinicians Arrange retrieval, transfer, and re-filing of medical records as required 4. Communication and telephone systems Receive and make telephone calls in accordance with practice policy, using clear communication and active listening Take accurate messages and ensure timely communication with clinicians and team members Ensure the telephone system is operational at the start of each day and switched to night service at the end of the day 5. Start and end of day procedures Open the premises at the start of the day, deactivate alarms, and prepare the practice to receive patients Secure the premises at the end of the day, ensuring the building is locked and alarms activated Be able to work shifts between 8.00am and 6.30pm as required 6. Professional responsibilities Maintain strict confidentiality at all times Demonstrate the ability to think independently, problem-solve, and manage competing priorities Use initiative, discretion, and common sense when responding to patient and operational issues Communicate effectively with colleagues, clinicians, and external organisations Maintain a clean, organised, and efficient working environment Communicate and work collaboratively with colleagues at all levels, treating others with professionalism, courtesy, and respect at all times. 7. Additional duties Undertake any other delegated duties appropriate to the role This job description outlines the main duties of the post and may be reviewed and amended in line with service needs.
